t: #2422 Merge Operations to Turn Array Into a Palindrome
o: Merging adjacent elements only ever grows one side's boundary value. Work inward with two pointers holding the current left block sum and right block sum: whichever side is smaller must absorb its neighbor (one operation), because a palindrome needs equal end blocks eventually. In [4,3,2,1,2,3,1]: left 4 vs right 1 → merge right (op 1, right=3); 4 vs 3 → merge right (op 2, right=4); equal → move both in; then 3 vs 3 equal, 2 vs 2 equal → done, 2 ops. For [1,2,3,4] everything collapses to one element: 3 ops.
k: Greedy two-pointer: always merge the smaller end sum into its neighbor.
Equal end sums consume both pointers with zero cost.
Each merge reduces the element count by 1, and the process terminates at a palindrome by construction.

a.n: Approach 1: Greedy two pointers on running sums
a.i: Maintain left/right partial sums. If left < right, the left block can never match the right block alone, so merge the next left element in (counts as one op); symmetrically for the other side; if equal, both boundaries are settled.
s: Set i=0, j=n−1, left=nums[0], right=nums[n−1], ops=0.
While i<j: if left<right, i++, left+=nums[i], ops++; elif left>right, j--, right+=nums[j], ops++; else i++, j-- and reset left/right to the new boundary values (if still i<j).
a.t: O(n) — each iteration advances i or j.

a.i: dp[l][r] = min merges to make nums[l..r] a palindrome; if ends are equal, dp[l][r]=dp[l+1][r−1]; otherwise dp[l][r]=1+min(dp[l+1][r], dp[l][r−1]). This is O(n²) and mainly useful to justify the greedy's correctness in discussion.
s: Fill by increasing interval length using the recurrence above.
a.t: O(n²) time and space — all intervals; too slow for n = 10⁵ in the worst case but correct.

w: Lead with the greedy two-pointer — it is optimal and simple. Pitfalls: resetting left/right sums after an equal match (and guarding i<j before reading nums[i]/nums[j]), and using 32-bit sums safely (values up to 10⁶ × 10⁵ fits in 64-bit; Python is unaffected). Follow-ups: prove greedy optimality by exchange argument; count the resulting palindrome's blocks.
